presets.title: The Climate Case for Nuclear
presets.description: Compare lifecycle CO2 and land use across all low-carbon sources.
presets.rhetoricalPoint: Nuclear's low-carbon credentials are underweighted in most climate conversations. Look at the numbers across CO2, land use, and how often each source actually generates power.

presets.title: Fear of Nuclear
presets.description: Deaths per terawatt-hour. Including mining, accidents, and air pollution.
presets.rhetoricalPoint: Nuclear is among the safest energy sources per unit produced. Coal kills hundreds of times more people per TWh, mostly from air pollution.

presets.title: Baseload vs Intermittent
presets.description: Capacity factor and load profile — the difference between energy and power.
presets.rhetoricalPoint: Baseload and intermittent sources are not interchangeable. Capacity factor measures how often a plant actually generates. Load profile tells you whether you can turn it on when you need it.

presets.title: The Cost Story
presets.description: Levelized cost of energy and how long it takes to build.
presets.rhetoricalPoint: Solar is cheapest unsubsidized per MWh. But LCOE alone misses storage costs, load profile, and the 60-80 year operating life of a nuclear plant compared to 25 years for solar panels.

presets.title: Land Hungry
presets.description: The spatial footprint of the energy transition.
presets.rhetoricalPoint: Powering a country with renewables requires hundreds of times more land than nuclear. This isn't an argument against renewables — it's a constraint on how the transition actually plays out.
